key_insight: κ-Ga₂O₃ thin films have low cross-plane thermal conductivity with weak thickness dependence, consistent with most intrinsic phonon mean free paths being shorter than the investigated film thicknesses.
engineering_relevance: κ-Ga₂O₃ electronics may require high-thermal-conductivity substrates or other heat-removal strategies to mitigate self-heating.
method: Frequency-domain thermoreflectance on (001) κ-Ga₂O₃ films grown on c-plane sapphire.
Thickness-dependent measurements from 159–689 nm and temperature-dependent measurements from 293–400 K.
First-principles-based calculations incorporating phonon–phonon and phonon–boundary scattering.
evidence_signal: Thermal conductivity increased from 1.83 (+0.19/−0.18) to 2.26 (+0.35/−0.40) W/(m·K) between 159 and 689 nm, with calculations capturing the weak size dependence.
watch_item: These cross-plane results for sapphire-supported films do not directly establish in-plane heat transport or device-level thermal performance.
paper_title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
